children.text: Tippe top

Model a tippe top as an axisymmetric truncated sphere of radius R with a stem. Its centre of mass C is displaced from geometric centre O by αR along the axis, with 0<α<1. Before the stem touches, the floor contact A satisfies \(\mathbf a=\overrightarrow{CA}=\alpha R\hat3-R\hat z\). The inertial XYZ frame has Z upward. The intermediate xyz frame rotates about Z by azimuth φ, with z=Z and symmetry axis \(\hat3=\sin\theta\hat x+\cos\theta\hat z\). Tilting xyz about y by θ gives the 123 frame, with 2=y and \(\hat1=\cos\theta\hat x-\sin\theta\hat z\). The axial spin angle is ψ. Principal inertias are I1=I2 and I3. The top has mass m, centre position s and sliding contact velocity vA=vx xhat+vy yhat. Kinetic friction is \(\mathbf F_f=-\mu_kN\mathbf v_A/|\mathbf v_A|\) when sliding, and the normal force is N. Initially the top is spun without a translational impulse. Unless asked otherwise consider θ<π/2 and no stem contact. The rotating derivative rule is \((d\mathbf A/dt)_{inertial}=(d\mathbf A/dt)_{rot}+\boldsymbol\omega_{frame}\times\mathbf A\).

children.text: Tippe top
a.1. Force diagram

\[\mathbf F_{ext}=(N-mg)\hat z+\mathbf F_f.\] Weight acts at C downward, N acts at A upward, and tangential friction acts at A opposite vA. The xy sketch must show opposite vA and Ff arrows. No absolute horizontal direction is prescribed.
a.2. Torque about centre of mass

Gravity has no torque about C. The contact torque is \(\boldsymbol\tau=\mathbf a\times(N\hat z+\mathbf F_f)\), or \[\tau_x=R(1-\alpha\cos\theta)F_{f,y},\quad\tau_y=R(\alpha\cos\theta-1)F_{f,x}-\alpha RN\sin\theta,\quad\tau_z=\alpha R\sin\theta F_{f,y}.\]
a.3. No vertical contact velocity

The material velocity at contact is \(\mathbf v_A=\dot{\mathbf s}+\boldsymbol\omega\times\mathbf a\). Although a labels the instantaneous geometric contact rather than one fixed material point, \(\dot{\mathbf a}=\alpha R\dot{\hat3}\) and \(\dot{\hat3}=\boldsymbol\omega\times\hat3\). The difference between adot and ω×a is horizontal. Therefore \(\mathbf v_A\cdot\hat z=(\dot{\mathbf s}+\dot{\mathbf a})\cdot\hat z=d[(\mathbf s+\mathbf a)\cdot\hat z]/dt=0\).
a.4. Angular velocity in both frames

Add the precession, tilt and spin: \(\boldsymbol\omega=\dot\phi\hat z+\dot\theta\hat2+\dot\psi\hat3\). Thus \[\boldsymbol\omega=\dot\psi\sin\theta\hat x+\dot\theta\hat y+(\dot\phi+\dot\psi\cos\theta)\hat z\] and \[\boldsymbol\omega=-\dot\phi\sin\theta\hat1+\dot\theta\hat2+(\dot\psi+\dot\phi\cos\theta)\hat3.\]
a.5. Energy in contact variables

\(U_g=mgR(1-\alpha\cos\theta)\), \(K_R=[I_1(\dot\theta^2+\dot\phi^2\sin^2\theta)+I_3(\dot\psi+\dot\phi\cos\theta)^2]/2\). The centre velocity is \[\dot{\mathbf s}=[v_x+R\dot\theta(1-\alpha\cos\theta)]\hat x+[v_y-R\sin\theta(\alpha\dot\phi+\dot\psi)]\hat y+\alpha R\dot\theta\sin\theta\hat z.\] Hence KT=m|sdot|²/2 and ET=KT+KR+Ug. Squaring the displayed components gives the requested explicit expression.
a.6. Vertical angular momentum rate
The z axis is fixed in inertial space, so \(\dot L_z=\tau_z=\alpha R\sin\theta F_{f,y}\).
a.7. Energy transfer and dissipation

Contact-force power splits into centre work \((N\hat z+\mathbf F_f)\cdot\dot{\mathbf s}\) and torque power \(\boldsymbol\tau\cdot\boldsymbol\omega\). Their sum is contact power \((N\hat z+\mathbf F_f)\cdot\mathbf v_A\). Since vAz=0, \[\dot E_T=\mathbf F_f\cdot\mathbf v_A=-\mu_kN|\mathbf v_A|\le0.\] Gravity exchanges kinetic and potential energy, with \(\dot U_g=mg\alpha R\sin\theta\dot\theta\). The normal force can do centre-of-mass work but has zero total rigid-body power at contact. Frictional Fy and its x,z torque components change vertical angular momentum and facilitate spin-to-tilt energy transfer. Friction dissipates total energy while rotational energy supplies the gravitational rise.
a.8. Energy sketches through inversion

ET decreases under sliding friction and approaches the final gravitational energy at rest. Ug rises during inversion and becomes constant when the stem-supported height settles. KT starts near zero, rises transiently and returns near zero in phase IV and to zero in V. KR is initially dominant, decreases overall as energy is transferred and dissipated, and vanishes in V. The source sketches it monotonically falling as a qualitative typical history, rather than a theorem for every possible trajectory. Draw all components consistently with ET=Ug+KT+KR. The spherical-contact formula for Ug ceases to apply once support transfers to the stem.
a.9. Transverse inertia identity
Axisymmetry gives \(\mathbf L=I_1\boldsymbol\omega+(I_3-I_1)(\boldsymbol\omega\cdot\hat3)\hat3\). Cross with 3hat: the second term vanishes and k=I1.
a.10. Jellett integral

Choose \(\mathbf v=\mathbf a=\alpha R\hat3-R\hat z\), or its negative, which changes only the convention for λ. Then \[\dot\lambda=\dot{\mathbf L}\cdot\mathbf a+\alpha R\mathbf L\cdot(\boldsymbol\omega\times\hat3).\] The first term vanishes because contact torque is a×F. By A9, \(\boldsymbol\omega\times\hat3=(\mathbf L\times\hat3)/I_1\), so the second term also vanishes. It is essential to differentiate the moving vector a: torque perpendicular to a alone would not prove conservation.
